lastCompletedGameRecap.recapHeadline: Jayden Daniels rallies Commanders in final seconds to set up winning kick in 22-20 win over Bengals
lastCompletedGameRecap.recapLeadExcerpt: LANDOVER, Md.  -- — Jayden Daniels and the Commanders had scored on five consecutive drives, all of them covering 50 yards or more.  But their last possession was the most daunting.  After the Cincinnati Bengals took a one-point lead on a 56-yard field goal by Evan McPherson , Washington took over at its 28-yard line with 39 seconds left and no timeouts. ” The game got off to a slow start in unexpected rainy conditions, but opened up in the second half as the teams traded scores throughout the third quarter.

injuryReport.name: Hjalte Froholdt
factors: Officially ruled Out on weekly game status report
injuryReport.beatComment: Froholdt was a full practice participant both Thursday and Friday, and he's progressed enough in his recovery to clear the league's concussion protocol. With Jon Gaines (ankle) ruled out, Froholdt should reclaim his starting job at center for Sunday's road tilt.

injuryReport.name: Carson Beck
factors: Did Not Participate (DNP) on Wednesday; remains sidelined from practice
injuryReport.beatComment: Beck hasn't practice since last Thursday, when his back spasms flared up, and he's now in danger of missing a second consecutive game Sunday against the Commanders. Ultimately, Friday's session and the Cardinals' ensuing injury report will dictate if Beck has a chance to play this weekend. Josh Johnson is waiting in the wings if Beck can't suit up.

injuryReport.name: Cody Simon
factors: Wednesday Limited Participation (LP); player toughness prior = 81%
injuryReport.beatComment: Simon is being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's contest. His absence gives the Cardinals less depth at linebacker behind Jack Gibbens, Mack Wilson and Zaven Collins.

injuryReport.name: Budda Baker
injuryReport.beatComment: Baker was able to register at least six stops for the fourth week in a row and seventh time overall this year. The safety is about as steady as they come, compiling 74 total tackles (36 solo), including a career-high 3.5 sacks, while also adding an interception and a forced fumble over 11 contests so far during the 2026 season.

injuryReport.name: Mack Wilson Sr.
factors: Habitual Veteran Rest prior (Mack Wilson Sr. maintenance schedule)
injuryReport.beatComment: Wilson was able to register at least eight stops for the second straight week and fifth time overall this season. The linebacker has now compiled 80 total tackles (35 solo), two passes defensed and a forced fumble over 11 contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

irReserve.name: Jeremiyah Love
factors: On Injured Reserve — 21-day practice window not yet opened
irReserve.beatComment: Love must miss at least one more game due to the right high-ankle sprain that he picked up in a Week 8 win at Dallas, but the Cardinals have a decision to make next week, as they have a Week 13 matchup with the Eagles on tap before a Week 14 bye. For as long as Love is sidelined, Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight will continue to man Arizona's backfield.

coachingMatchup.headline: Dan Quinn & DC Daronte Jones vs. HC Mike LaFleur, OC Nathaniel Hackett & DC Nick Rallis (Road Test)
coachingMatchup.summary: Week 12 two-sided coordinator chess match pitting Washington Commanders's staff (Dan Quinn, OC David Blough, DC Daronte Jones) against Arizona Cardinals (3-8)—testing both Washington's offensive efficiency and its defensive pass-rush and coverage discipline.
bullets: Pass-Game Efficiency & Coverage Shell Delta: Dan Quinn and OC David Blough pair condensed splits with pre-snap jet motion and orbit motion to stress Arizona Cardinals's single-high vs. two-high rotations—widening curl/flat defenders to attack the honey-hole between hook/curl linebackers and deep safeties on play-action choice/dagger concepts.

Trench Run-Fit & Two-Way Leverage: Against Arizona Cardinals's pin-and-pull, counter, and duo runs targeting the A- and B-gaps, DC Daronte Jones balances four-man pressure with disguised Quarters and Cover 6 split-safety rotations on early downs and in the red zone.

Money-Down & Red-Zone Execution: Third-down conversion discipline and red-zone touchdown rate govern whether Washington sustains multi-play scoring drives or yields momentum to Arizona Cardinals's pass rush and coverage disguises.
Tempo, Turnovers & Venue Leverage: Road Test situational play-calling, penalty margin, and turnover differential provide the clearest late-game swing factors for both coaching staffs.

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Jayden Daniels, Chig Okonkwo & Antonio Williams vs. CB Kalen King & LB Jack Gibbens
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: WAS: #19 Pass Off (217.0 yds) · #17 Off. Scoring (+0.46) | ARI: #31 Pass Def (+7.78)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Jayden Daniels, Chig Okonkwo & Antonio Williams attack the intermediate seams and middle-of-the-field leverage windows against Arizona Cardinals's #31 pass defense (+7.78). Winning early-down timing throws keeps Washington's offense ahead of the chains and punishes disguised single-high rotations.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch Jayden Daniels (#5) scanning Cardinals's deep safeties at the snap—when LB Jack Gibbens widens to take away the crossers, the intermediate seam opens immediately for Chig Okonkwo (#85).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Charles Omenihu, Dorance Armstrong & Tim Settle vs. QB Joey Aguilar & OT Josh Fryar
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: WAS: #16 Def Sacks (2.3/gm) | ARI: #16 Pass Protection (6.5%)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Charles Omenihu, Dorance Armstrong & Tim Settle lead Washington's #16 NFL pass rush (2.3/gm) against Arizona Cardinals's #16 pass-protection unit (6.5%). Collapsing the interior pocket without sending extra blitzers lets Commanders keep seven defenders in coverage.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: On 3rd-and-6+, watch whether Charles Omenihu (#90) draw chip help from Cardinals's tight ends or backs—creating 1-on-1 rush lanes inside for Dorance Armstrong (#92).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Nick Cross, Amik Robertson & Frankie Luvu vs. WR Simi Fehoko & QB Joey Aguilar
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: WAS: #20 Pass Def (+2.63) | ARI: #23 Pass Off (196.1 yds)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Nick Cross, Amik Robertson & Frankie Luvu anchor Washington's #20 pass defense (+2.63) against WR Simi Fehoko and Arizona Cardinals's #23 passing attack (196.1 yds). Limiting explosive 20+ yard chunk plays forces Cardinals into sustained red-zone drives.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Track Nick Cross (#25) at the top of routes against WR Simi Fehoko: press-bail alignment with safety help over the top takes away QB Joey Aguilar's preferred isolation shots.

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Rachaad White & Stefon Diggs vs. Cardinals Front Seven & LB Jack Gibbens
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: WAS: #11 Rush Off (120.1 yds) | ARI: #11 Rush Def (-1.09)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Rachaad White & Stefon Diggs test Arizona Cardinals's #11 run defense (-1.09) with horizontal stretch and interior cutback lanes. Generating 4.5+ yards on first down unlocks play-action explosives and neutralizes Cardinals's pass-rush packages.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch whether Cardinals's linebackers over-pursue motion to the perimeter—opening decisive backside B-gap cutback lanes for Rachaad White (#1).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Josh Conerly Jr., Chris Paul & Sam Cosmi vs. DT Roy Lopez & Cardinals Simulated Pressures
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: WAS: #16 Pass Protection (6.0%) | ARI: #16 Def Sacks (2.4/gm)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Josh Conerly Jr., Chris Paul & Sam Cosmi protect Jayden Daniels (#16 protection at 6.0%) against DT Roy Lopez and Arizona Cardinals's #16 pass rush (2.4/gm). Passing off interior twists and simulated blitzes cleanly determines late-down conversion efficiency.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch Josh Conerly Jr. (#72) on obvious passing downs—if DT Roy Lopez cannot win clean around the arc, Cardinals must dial up interior stunts that stress Chris Paul (#75).
